bull.b: Product-led growth is more durable than one-off licensing revenue because it reflects customer shipments and adoption of Sequans technology. Continued volume expansion could improve scale economics as IoT programs mature.

Conversion of design wins into mass production provides visibility beyond the current quarter and validates product-market fit. A growing production base can support recurring chipset demand and strengthen Sequans' position with OEMs.

Debt repayment reduces financing obligations and refinancing risk, giving management greater flexibility to fund product development and customer programs. The stronger balance sheet also provides more time to pursue the stated path toward breakeven.

bear.b: Sequans has not yet demonstrated self-funded operations, and substantial losses can consume its liquidity before product scaling delivers breakeven. Sustained cash burn may require further financing or asset monetization to support growth.

Lower product margins limit operating leverage and make profitability more dependent on volume growth and cost controls. Persistent component constraints could raise input costs, delay shipments, or weaken customer economics across the production pipeline.

Dependence on uncertain licensing and services timing creates revenue volatility and reduces visibility into quarterly performance. It also complicates the breakeven plan because product growth may not alone cover the current expense base.
